Book correction: The definition sentence is garbled ('Let ... be any equation ... is called') and says 'for some real number k'. It should read: an equation f(x, y) = 0 in two variables x and y is called a homogeneous equation of degree n (a positive integer) if the function f(x, y) is homogeneous of degree n, that is, f(kx, ky) = k^{n}f(x, y) for every real number k. ('For some k' is not enough: k = 1 works for e

Book correction: The book prints the last term inside the bracket as m_{1}m_{2}x^{3} and puts '= 0' after the bracket. Equation (v) has m_{1}m_{2}x^{2}, and the bracket is f(x, y) itself (not 0), so the line should read: = k^{2}[y^{2} - (m_{1}+m_{2})xy + m_{1}m_{2}x^{2}] \Rightarrow f(kx, ky) = k^{2}f(x, y)
